test_title: PYST 38: SSC MTS - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 21 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 15% and 20% on an article and is still able to earn a 70% profit. If he offers a single discount of 30%, what will his profit percentage be?
solution:
**Given:**

Successive discounts = 15% and 20%

Profit = 70%

Single Discount = 30%

**Concept Used:**

Selling Price = (100+Profit\%)/(100)times CP

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the cost price of an article be Rs 100

⇒ Price after first discount of 15% = 100 – 15% of 100

⇒ Selling price after first discount of 15% = 100-(15)/(100)times 100=100-15=85 Rs

⇒ Price after second discount of 20% = 85 – 20% of 85

⇒ Final Selling Price = 85-(20)/(100)times 85=85-17=68 Rs

⇒ Now, Cost Price = (100)/(100+70)times 68=(10)/(17)times 68=40 Rs

⇒ So, to sell the article at 30% discount,

⇒ Selling Price = 100-(30)/(100)times 100=100-30=70 Rs

⇒ Profit = SP – CP = 70 – 40 = Rs 30

⇒ Then, Profit Percentage = (Profit)/(CP)times 100=(30)/(40)times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 75%

**Hence, the profit percentage made on single discount of 30% is 75%.**
